title: Hosted KV concurrency fuzzcase repro notes
content:
Summary:
This is a working notes doc for a reproducible concurrency fuzzcase that surfaced a latent KV cache race leading to transient host-level OOMs and continuous-batching starvation. The goal here is to capture the minimal repro, telemetry we used, experiments attempted, and a first-pass runbook sketch for on-call to contain and mitigate while engineering ships a fix.

Why this is different from recent KV incidents:
- Not a persistent corruption or eviction-index misalignment. The failure mode appears when aggressive concurrent reads + asynchronous prefetch + partial eviction races happen on certain host memory layouts.
- Triggers at medium QPS for long context (>= 8k tokens) workloads in Dedicated-like tenants where KV spillback and prefix caching are both enabled.

Observed symptoms (customer and infra):
- Short window (30–90s) of sustained heap growth on 2–4 hosts followed by OOM kills.
- Batching latency spikes (p99 increases from ~120ms to ~600ms) and microbatch starvation signaled in telemetry.
- SREs see large numbers of in-flight async prefetch futures pending and backlog of cache-rebuild events.
- No consistent single code-path crash; host may survive after GC flurry but KV entries remain partially rebuilt (rebuild TTLs extended).

Initial timeline (UTC):
- 2024-09-29 14:02: upstream alert: host memory exceeded 90% for host-gpu-12
- 2024-09-29 14:03: p95/p99 latency alert for route /v1/generate triggered
- 2024-09-29 14:04: host-gpu-12 OOM kill, process restarted by k8s
- 2024-09-29 14:05: similar pattern observed for host-gpu-15 and host-gpu-22 within 3 minutes
- 2024-09-29 14:08: on-call paged. Began capture of heap profiles and live pstack from restarted hosts.
- 2024-09-29 14:20: triage note: concurrent prefetch/backfill queue size ballooning in logs, eviction thrash events 42x baseline

Telemetry & artifacts captured:
- heap profiles: s3://infra-artifacts/kv-fuzz/host-gpu-12-1408.heap (samples at 14:05, 14:06, 14:07)
- flamegraphs: s3://infra-artifacts/kv-fuzz/fg-host-gpu-12-1406.svg
- trace snapshots: trace-id: 0b1f-evict-20240929-14:06
- logs: /var/log/redwood/serving-runtime/host-gpu-12/oom-window*.log
- reproduction harness: local gist: https://gist.github.com/lydiapark/hosted-kv-fuzz-repro

Minimal repro (what reproduced locally for SRE/eng):
- Run the repro harness against a 4-host local cluster (docker-compose variant included in gist). The harness does:
  - spawn 160 concurrent clients issuing mix of: 70% read, 25% prefetch(triggered by synthetic prompts that produce long KV prefixes), 5% write (small metadata updates)
  - use sequence lengths = 8192 +/- 1024 tokens to stress KV growth
  - artificially lower the KV rebuild-worker concurrency parameter to replicate backlog (cfg: kv.rebuild_worker_count=3)
- After ~3–6 minutes the harness reliably reproduces: sustained heap growth on 1–2 replica processes and eviction thrash logs.
- Repro commands: (local)
  - ./scripts/bootstrap-local-cluster --hosts 4 --gpus 0 --mode dev
  - python tools/kv_fuzz_harness.py --clients 160 --seq-len 8192 --duration 600 --prefetch-rate 0.25

Notes about reproducer and caveats:
- Reproducer depends on non-default config (prefetch+spillback enabled). It will not reproduce on a fresh minimal serving config.
- Host-level OOMs require long-context workloads; unit tests won't catch this.
- The reproducer is intentionally noisy; when reducing concurrency below ~40 clients the issue disappears.

Hypotheses explored and quick outcomes:
1) Double-checked for KV-entry size accounting bug (were we double-counting during async prefetch?).
   - grep + counters: no evidence of double-counting in recent builds. Counter consistency checks OK.
2) Race between eviction iterator and async prefetch insertion leaving orphaned references that prevent GC.
   - instrumented eviction path with refcounts -> saw short-lived refcount spikes where refcount never dropped to zero until rebuild completed. Suggests temporary reference leakage.
3) Rebuild queue backlog amplifies memory because entries are kept in rebuild-in-progress state and pinned in KV hash table.
   - throttling rebuild_worker_count reduced pressure but increased latency for cold requests (tradeoff).
4) Contention on per-shard locks combined with prefetch futures holding onto partial buffers.
   - flamegraphs show long waits on shard mutex during eviction; buffer allocations held while waiting.

Mitigations experimented (lab & prod-safe knobs):
- Immediate prod-safe mitigations (on-call actionable):
  1) Toggle feature flag that disables async prefetch for affected tenant(s): api toggle FF_kv_async_prefetch=false (observed immediate drop in rebuild backlog and memory pressure).
  2) Scale down kv.rebuild_worker_count to 2 across hosts to reduce simultaneous working set (templated dynconfig change rolled in 2 mins). Observed lower memory but higher cold-miss p50.
  3) Apply temporary eviction-aggressiveness increase: kv.eviction_threshold_percent=65 (default 80) to free memory quickly. Todo: this increases TTL churn.
- Engineering experiments (not for on-call):
  - Patch: add ephemeral guard that converts prefetch futures to streaming prefetched chunks and yield if worker backlog > N. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987 (linked). Local tests show no OOM under fuzz harness and only ~8% latency regression.
  - Patch: stronger per-entry GC handoff to prevent orphan refs; requires deeper refactor of KV entry lifecycle. Prototype branch: feature/kv-gc-handoff.

Runbook sketch (for SRE playbook inclusion) — top-level steps when paging for similar alerts:
1) Pager triage checklist:
   - Confirm host OOM pattern: check k8s events + syslog for OOM kill timestamps.
   - Correlate with telemetry: high eviction-thrash metric, rebuild-queue-length, prefetch-pending-count.
   - Identify tenant(s) and routes by checking recent allocation and request traces.
2) Immediate containment (fast):
   - Toggle FF_kv_async_prefetch=false for affected tenant(s) (Feature Flag rollback).
   - If feature flag unavailable, adjust dynconfig: set kv.rebuild_worker_count=2 and kv.eviction_threshold_percent=65.
   - Add temporary routing rule to divert heavy long-context traffic to fallback model variant (lower context) if that tenant and route exist.
3) Memory triage (post-containment):
   - Gather heap profile and flamegraph within 5 minutes of containment. Upload to s3 path and annotate incident ticket.
   - Enable increased eviction sampling for 10 minutes to get more data.
4) Recovery verification:
   - Watch host memory for 10 minutes; ensure no new OOMs and batching latency returns to baseline p95 within 20 minutes.

Longer-term engineering follow-ups and owners:
- Implement per-entry ephemeral weak references to ensure prefetch doesn’t pin buffers (owner: eng-serving-runtime / Marcus Chen) — JIRA-1234.
- Add C++ sanitizer-style fuzz harness to CI that runs the kv_fuzz_harness against the dev 4-host cluster nightly (owner: eng-sre / Lydia Park).
- Add metric: kv.prefetch_pending_by_shard and alert when > 1000 per-shard for > 60s (owner: observability / Anjali Rao).
- Revisit default for kv.rebuild_worker_count and eviction_threshold in Dedicated to be conservative for long-context workloads (owner: product/dedicated).

Open questions & unknowns:
- Why are only a subset of hosts affected within a pool? Hypothesis: host memory layout + past allocation patterns (noise from other tenants) amplify the leak. Need host-level reproducibility testing.
- Is there a latent interaction with NUMA binding on Dedicated hosts? We need to run repro with NUMA-affinity toggles.
- Could the prefetch buffer size auto-tuning be growing unbounded under certain input distributions? Capture samples of buffer sizes in next run.

Notes to self (short-term checklist):
- [ ] Upload all heap/fg/trace artifacts to incident JIRA ticket and tag owners.
- [ ] Land the prod-safe FF revert script in ops-runbooks repo (small PR).
- [ ] Add kv_fuzz_harness to nightly job matrix behind a canary.
- [ ] Schedule 1-hour postmortem session with eng-serving-runtime + eng-sre next week.

Appendix: quick diagnostic commands (on-call cheatsheet)
- Check OOM events: kubectl get events --field-selector reason=OOMKilling -n serving --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 30
- Host memory time-series (last 30m): datapoint query in Grafana: hosts.memory.usage_bytes{host=~"host-gpu-.*"}[30m]
- Rebuild queue length by host: sum by(host) (metric: kv_rebuild_queue_length)
- Snapshot heap profile: curl -sS localhost:6060/debug/heap > /tmp/host-heap-$(date +%s).heap && aws s3 cp /tmp/host-heap-*.heap s3://infra-artifacts/kv-fuzz/
- Toggle FF: curl -X POST $FF_ADMIN/toggle -d '{"flag":"FF_kv_async_prefetch","value":false,"tenant":"TENANT"}'

If you're reading this mid-incident: ping @eng-serving-runtime on Slack, mention JIRA-1234, and follow the checklist above. Comments, corrections, and additional repro cases welcome — leave them in this doc or the linked PR/Slack thread.

-- Lydia
